An estimated 905,000 Rohingya refugees currently reside in Cox`s Bazar, Bangladesh, over 700,000 of whom fled extreme violence in Myanmar in late 2017. They reside in refugee camps, which are among the most congested camps in the world, with limited access to basic services, including adequate sanitation, healthcare, livelihoods and education.
The refugees have put an immense strain on the Bangladeshi`s living in Cox`s Bazar, however, despite the challenges, the Bangladeshi communities were the first to respond when the Rohingya arrived and generously continue to host the refugees, and many of the local communities are now also in need of support.
NRC has been present in Bangladesh since 2016, working through partnerships with local NGO`s. We have since scaled up our presence in Bangladesh, obtaining legal registration in November 2018, allowing us to better respond to the Rohingya influx. Alongside our partners, we provide assistance to refugees and local communities through Education programming and Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) activities.

job_description: Duty Station: Camp 5 and 12, Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar Reports to: MIS Manager Accountable to: Project Coordinator Position Summary The Surveillance Officer plays an important role in systematic collection, verification, analysis, interpretation, reporting, and follow-up of health information and disease surveillance. This position involves implementing routine disease surveillance activities to identify, investigate, and monitor disease patterns, outbreaks, emerging health threats, and other public health risks. The Officer is responsible for ensuring timely, accurate, and complete surveillance reporting and sharing information with the Epidemiologist and relevant stakeholders to support early warning, preparedness, response, and disease prevention and control. The Surveillance Officer will work closely with the Epidemiologist, Health Information Systems (HIS) team, MEAL Manager, Project Coordinator, health facility departments, Community Health Workers (CHWs), and relevant government, Health Sector, humanitarian, and partner stakeholders to strengthen surveillance systems, data quality, reporting, and timely public health action. Key Responsibilities KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY: Disease Surveillance, Outbreaks, Epidemiological Analysis & Data Management Implement routine disease surveillance activities at assigned health facilities and ensure timely verification, reporting, and follow-up of surveillance information to identify trends, patterns, potential outbreaks, and priority public health concerns. Monitor priority diseases, syndromes, unusual health events, emerging threats, and other reportable conditions through EWARS, DHIS2, HIS/HMIS, and other relevant reporting systems. Provide verified surveillance data for programme, management, donor, and humanitarian reporting. Maintain regular communication with relevant programme, technical, government, Health Sector, partner, and stakeholders regarding surveillance findings and emerging health threats. Perform any other duties as assigned by the supervisor. Research, Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting Prepare surveillance summaries, which includes, however not limited to, situational analyses, epidemiological briefs, updates, tables, charts, graphs, and dashboards to support programme and management decision-making. Assist in the preparation of technical briefs, bulletins, reports, research outputs, and publications. Support data collection, analysis, documentation, and field-level implementation of epidemiological and public health research. (Active data collection might be required) Conduct field investigations, rapid assessments, active case findings, and other epidemiological investigations when required. Monitor surveillance implementation, data quality, reporting practices, and compliance with surveillance procedures and follow up on action points. Maintain documentation of surveillance, outbreak investigation, response activities, findings, and follow-up actions. Health Information Systems & Coordination Conduct routine data quality checks and verify consistency between source documents, surveillance databases, health information systems, and submitted reports in coordination with HIS/ MEAL team. Identify and follow up data gaps, inconsistencies, delays, and reporting issues with responsible departments. Participate in relevant surveillance, health, epidemiology, outbreak, and coordination meetings and contribute surveillance findings as required. Field Support, Capacity Building & Knowledge Management and Knowledge Translation Provide orientation and technical support to health facility staff (technical/ non-technical) on surveillance tools, case definitions, reporting procedures, information requirements and data requirements. Disseminate key surveillance findings, trends, alerts, and public health concerns to relevant health facility and programme teams. Promote awareness of priority diseases, surveillance requirements, and timely reporting among relevant health facility and community-level staff. Emergency Preparedness & Response Maintain readiness to support disease surveillance and information management during outbreaks and other humanitarian emergencies. Support rapid surveillance, data collection, analysis, reporting, and information management during disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies. Provide timely surveillance information to support emergency decision-making, response planning, and risk communication. Remain flexible and responsive to urgent surveillance and public health requirements during emergencies. job_description: Duty Station:  Camp 5 & 21, Cox’s Bazar Reports to:  Clinical Coordinator Accountable to:  Deputy Project Coordinator Position Summary The Senior Medical Officer (Sr. Medical Officer) will be responsible for providing safe, high-quality, timely, and patient-centred medical care at the Primary Health Care Centre (PHCC) in the Rohingya Response, Cox’s Bazar. The position holder will provide clinical assessment, diagnosis, treatment, emergency management, stabilization, referral, and follow-up of patients in accordance with approved national guidelines, Health Sector standards, organizational protocols, and professional medical ethics. The Senior Medical Officer will also provide day-to-day clinical guidance and technical support to Medical Officers and other assigned healthcare personnel. The position holder will support clinical quality assurance, patient safety, Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), clinical documentation, disease surveillance, referral systems, emergency preparedness, and continuity of care. The Sr. Medical Officer will work closely with the Clinical Coordinator/Clinical In-Charge, Medical Officers, Senior Staff Nurses, Staff Nurses, Midwife Lead, Midwives, Pharmacy, Laboratory, Nutrition, MHPSS, Community Health, MEAL, and other relevant teams to ensure integrated and comprehensive primary healthcare services. Key Responsibilities Clinical Care & Patient Management Provide comprehensive, safe, respectful, and patient-centred medical care to patients attending the PHCC. Conduct thorough clinical assessment, history taking, physical examination, diagnosis, and treatment within the scope of PHCC services. Develop appropriate treatment and management plans based on approved clinical guidelines and protocols. Prescribe medicines and treatments rationally and appropriately. Manage common communicable and non-communicable diseases according to approved guidelines. Ensure appropriate management of patients with acute and chronic medical conditions. Identify patients requiring additional investigation, observation, specialist consultation, or referral. Provide appropriate follow-up instructions and continuity of care. Ensure patient dignity, privacy, confidentiality, informed consent, and non-discriminatory care at all times. Primary Healthcare Service Delivery Support the delivery of comprehensive primary healthcare services in accordance with the approved Essential Package of Health Services. Provide consultation and treatment for common medical conditions among children, adolescents, adults, and older persons. Support the management of communicable and non-communicable diseases. Ensure appropriate screening, diagnosis, treatment, counselling, and follow-up. Support integrated healthcare services in coordination with nursing, maternal health, nutrition, MHPSS, laboratory, pharmacy, and community health teams. Identify health conditions requiring specialized care and ensure appropriate referral. Promote continuity and accessibility of essential healthcare services. Clinical Assessment, Diagnosis & Treatment Conduct appropriate clinical assessments and establish differential and final diagnoses. Request and interpret relevant laboratory investigations within the scope of available services. Ensure evidence-based and rational clinical decision-making. Follow approved national treatment guidelines, standard treatment protocols, and organizational clinical procedures. Monitor patient response to treatment and modify management plans when clinically appropriate. Identify complications, treatment failure, or deterioration requiring escalation or referral. Ensure appropriate counselling of patients and caregivers regarding diagnosis, treatment, medication use, and follow-up. Emergency Care & Stabilization Provide immediate medical assessment and emergency management for patients presenting with acute or life-threatening conditions. Identify and manage medical emergencies within the capacity of the PHCC. Provide initial stabilization of critically ill patients before referral. Coordinate with nursing staff and other healthcare personnel during emergency situations. Ensure timely escalation and referral of patients requiring higher-level care. Support emergency management of medical, paediatric, neonatal, and other relevant emergencies within the scope of the PHCC. Ensure appropriate emergency documentation and communication during patient transfer. Participate in emergency preparedness activities, drills, and response. Triage & Patient Prioritization Support appropriate clinical triage and prioritization of patients according to clinical urgency. Identify danger signs and patients requiring immediate medical attention. Ensure prompt assessment of critically ill or deteriorating patients. Support nursing and clinical staff in identifying emergency conditions. Monitor patient flow and contribute to reducing unnecessary delays in access to care. Ensure appropriate escalation and management of high-risk patients. Referral & Continuity of Care Assess patients requiring referral to higher-level healthcare facilities. Ensure appropriate clinical stabilization before referral whenever possible. Complete accurate and comprehensive referral documentation. Communicate relevant clinical information to referral facilities when required. Provide appropriate counselling to patients and caregivers regarding referral procedures. Coordinate with the Clinical Coordinator/Clinical In-Charge and relevant teams regarding complex referrals. Support appropriate follow-up of referred patients when applicable. Monitor referral challenges and communicate significant concerns to the appropriate supervisor. Clinical Supervision & Technical Support Provide day-to-day clinical guidance and technical support to Medical Officers and assigned clinical personnel. Support junior medical staff in clinical assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and patient management. Provide guidance regarding complex or challenging clinical cases. Conduct case discussions and clinical reviews. Support newly recruited medical staff through orientation and on-the-job mentoring. Monitor adherence to clinical guidelines, treatment protocols, and professional standards. Identify knowledge and performance gaps and provide appropriate coaching. Escalate significant clinical, performance, or professional concerns to the Clinical Coordinator or appropriate supervisor. Clinical Quality & Quality Improvement Ensure medical services are delivered according to approved national guidelines, organizational protocols, and professional standards. Promote evidence-based clinical practice. Participate in clinical audits, case reviews, supportive supervision, and quality improvement activities. Review patient records, prescriptions, and clinical documentation to identify quality gaps. Support prescription audits and promote rational use of medicines. Identify clinical service delivery gaps and recommend corrective actions. Support implementation of quality improvement initiatives. Promote a culture of learning, accountability, patient safety, and continuous improvement. Patient Safety & Clinical Risk Management Promote patient safety across all clinical service areas. Identify and report clinical risks, adverse events, near misses, and unsafe practices. Support appropriate management and follow-up of clinical incidents. Ensure safe clinical decision-making and appropriate treatment practices. Promote safe medication prescribing and administration. Ensure appropriate patient identification and clinical documentation. Escalate serious patient safety concerns immediately through appropriate channels. Support corrective and preventive actions following clinical incidents. Medication Management & Rational Use of Medicines Prescribe medicines appropriately according to approved clinical guidelines and protocols. Promote rational and evidence-based use of medicines. Ensure prescriptions are clear, accurate, and complete. Consider patient allergies, contraindications, potential drug interactions, and other relevant clinical factors. Monitor patients for treatment response and possible adverse drug reactions. Coordinate with Pharmacy staff regarding medicine availability and medication-related concerns. Participate in prescription reviews and medication audits. Report significant medication-related incidents according to organizational procedures. Infection Prevention & Control (IPC) Follow and promote Infection Prevention and Control procedures in all assigned clinical areas. Ensure adherence to standard precautions and appropriate use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Promote appropriate hand hygiene practices. Support appropriate cleaning, disinfection, waste management, and environmental safety. Identify and report IPC risks, gaps, or breaches. Support the implementation of IPC measures during disease outbreaks and public health emergencies. Work closely with relevant teams to strengthen IPC compliance. Promote safe practices to protect patients, healthcare workers, and communities. Communicable Disease Management & Surveillance Diagnose and manage common communicable diseases according to approved guidelines. Maintain awareness of disease trends and public health risks within the PHCC catchment area. Identify unusual disease patterns, clusters, or suspected outbreaks. Ensure appropriate reporting of notifiable diseases and public health concerns through established channels. Support disease surveillance and outbreak response activities. Coordinate with relevant surveillance, laboratory, community health, and public health teams. Participate in outbreak preparedness and response activities when required. Non-Communicable Disease (NCD) Management Screen, diagnose, and manage common non-communicable diseases within the scope of PHCC services. Provide counselling on lifestyle modification and disease prevention. Support continuity of care for patients with chronic diseases. Monitor treatment response and medication adherence. Identify patients requiring specialized assessment or referral. Ensure appropriate documentation and follow-up of NCD patients. Maternal, Newborn & Child Health Support Work closely with Midwives, Midwife Lead, Nurses, and other relevant staff to support integrated maternal and child healthcare services. Provide medical assessment and management of pregnancy-related complications within the scope of the PHCC. Support emergency management and referral of obstetric complications. Support assessment and management of sick children. Identify and manage paediatric danger signs and emergencies. Support appropriate referral of high-risk mothers, newborns, and children. Participate in clinical case discussions involving maternal and child health. Coordination with Multidisciplinary Teams Work closely with the Clinical Coordinator/Clinical In-Charge, Medical Officers, Nursing team, Midwife Lead, Midwives, Pharmacy, Laboratory, Nutrition, MHPSS, Community Health, and other relevant teams. Promote integrated and multidisciplinary patient care. Coordinate patient investigations, treatment, referral, and follow-up. Participate in clinical meetings, case discussions, mortality reviews, and programme review meetings. Communicate clinical concerns and service delivery challenges to the appropriate supervisor. Support effective communication and teamwork across PHCC service areas. Coordinate with referral facilities and other healthcare providers when required. Clinical Documentation & Patient Records Maintain accurate, complete, timely, and confidential patient records. Ensure appropriate documentation of clinical assessments, diagnoses, treatment plans, prescriptions, investigations, referrals, and follow-up. Ensure clinical records are completed according to organizational and national requirements. Maintain confidentiality of patient information. Support regular review of clinical documentation. Identify documentation gaps and support staff in improving record quality. Ensure appropriate data protection procedures are followed. Laboratory & Diagnostic Services Coordination Request appropriate laboratory investigations based on clinical indications. Interpret available diagnostic results and incorporate findings into patient management. Coordinate with Laboratory staff regarding urgent investigations and significant results. Ensure appropriate clinical follow-up based on laboratory findings. Promote rational use of laboratory investigations. Identify diagnostic limitations affecting patient management and communicate these appropriately. Medicines, Medical Supplies & Equipment Coordinate with Pharmacy and relevant teams regarding essential medicines and clinical requirements. Identify potential medicine shortages affecting patient care. Support rational use of available medicines and medical supplies. Report shortages or critical gaps affecting clinical services. Ensure appropriate use and care of medical equipment. Identify unsafe, damaged, or non-functional equipment and report promptly. Support regular review of emergency medicines and essential clinical supplies. Health Information & Reporting Ensure accurate recording of patient consultations and clinical services. Maintain relevant clinical registers and patient records. Support the preparation of daily, weekly, monthly, and other required reports. Review clinical data for completeness, accuracy, and consistency. Support analysis of clinical trends and service utilization. Report unusual disease patterns, clinical incidents, and significant public health concerns. Coordinate with the Clinical Coordinator and MEAL/Health Information teams regarding reporting requirements. Maintain confidentiality of patient and programme information. Capacity Building & Professional Development Participate in clinical training, refresher sessions, case discussions, and professional development activities. Support on-the-job coaching and mentoring of Medical Officers and other assigned healthcare personnel. Share clinical knowledge and updated medical guidance with the team. Maintain updated knowledge of national clinical guidelines and relevant humanitarian health protocols. Participate in clinical learning and quality improvement initiatives. Promote continuous professional development within the clinical team. Emergency Preparedness & Humanitarian Response Maintain readiness to provide medical services during disease outbreaks, fires, natural disasters, mass casualty incidents, and other humanitarian emergencies. Participate in emergency preparedness planning and simulation exercises. Support continuity of essential PHCC services during emergencies. Provide medical support during emergency response activities. Support the organization and prioritization of patients during mass casualty incidents. Coordinate with relevant teams during emergency situations. Remain flexible to undertake additional responsibilities based on programme and emergency requirements. job_description: Job Description:  Midwife – PHCC, Camp 5, 12 and 21, Cox’s Bazar Position Summary Partners in Health and Development (PHD), in collaboration with Save the Children Bangladesh, provides emergency, maternal, neonatal, and child health services to Rohingya refugees and the surrounding host community through its health facilities in Cox’s Bazar. The Midwife will be responsible for providing quality, respectful, and evidence-based maternal and newborn health services in a field hospital setting. The position holder will support antenatal, intrapartum, postnatal, and immediate newborn care, including the management of normal deliveries, early identification of complications, emergency response, stabilization, and timely referral. The Midwife will work closely with Medical Officers, Nurses, Senior Midwives, and other multidisciplinary team members to ensure safe and comprehensive care for mothers and newborns in accordance with approved clinical protocols, infection prevention and control standards, and humanitarian principles. Duty Station: Camp 5, 12 and 21, Cox’s Bazar Reports to: Midwife Lead Accountable to: Clinical Coordinator KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:  1. Antenatal Care Provide routine antenatal care and assessment to pregnant women according to approved clinical guidelines and protocols. Monitor maternal health, including vital signs and fetal well-being. Identify high-risk pregnancies and danger signs and ensure timely consultation, referral, or escalation to the appropriate clinician. Provide counseling on nutrition, birth preparedness, danger signs, personal hygiene, and other essential maternal health issues. Support pregnant women and their families with appropriate health education and counseling. 2. Labour and Delivery Care Assess women presenting in labour and provide appropriate monitoring and care throughout the labour process. Conduct and manage normal vaginal deliveries according to approved clinical protocols. Monitor and accurately document the progress of labour using appropriate tools, including the partograph,WHO labor care guide where applicable. Monitor maternal and fetal vital signs during labour and delivery. Provide respectful maternity care while ensuring privacy, dignity, confidentiality, and informed consent. Identify complications and obstetric emergencies promptly and immediately notify the responsible Medical Officer or senior medical officer. Assist in the initial management and stabilization of obstetric emergencies, including postpartum haemorrhage, eclampsia, prolonged or obstructed labour, and other complications, within the scope of practice and established protocols. Assist the clinical team during complicated deliveries and emergency obstetric procedures when required. Practice & promote evidence-based care. Support in preparation before operative procedure. 3. Postnatal and Newborn Care Provide immediate postnatal care to mothers following delivery. Monitor mothers for postpartum complications and ensure timely referral or escalation when necessary. Conduct initial assessment and essential care of newborns immediately after birth. Support newborn thermal care, breastfeeding initiation, cord care, infection prevention, and other essential newborn care practices. Assist in newborn resuscitation and stabilization during emergencies according to training, clinical protocols, and scope of practice. Identify sick or high-risk newborns and ensure timely referral to the appropriate unit or clinician, including SCANU/NICU where available. Provide support and counseling to mothers and caregivers on breastfeeding, newborn care, hygiene, family planning, and postnatal danger signs. 4. Emergency and Referral Support Respond promptly and confidently to maternal and newborn emergencies. Assist with emergency stabilization and management within the scope of professional practice. Ensure timely communication with Medical Officers and other relevant clinical staff during emergency situations. Prepare and support patients for referral to higher-level facilities when required. Complete relevant referral documentation and maintain continuity of care. 5. Infection Prevention, Safety and Quality of Care Maintain strict infection prevention and control (IPC) practices in the labour room, maternity ward, and other assigned areas. Ensure proper cleaning, sterilization, and safe handling of medical equipment and supplies. Follow waste management and occupational health and safety procedures. Maintain patient safety, confidentiality, dignity, and respectful maternity care at all times. Follow organizational policies, clinical guidelines, SOPs, and relevant national and international standards. 6. Documentation and Reporting Maintain accurate and timely patient records, including ANC, labour, delivery, postnatal, newborn, referral, and other relevant registers. Ensure complete documentation of assessments, care provided, outcomes, complications, and referrals. Support the preparation of daily, weekly, and monthly service data and reports as required. Maintain confidentiality and proper management of patient information and medical records. Report maternal, newborn, or other significant clinical incidents, maternal and perinatal death,high risk cases according to organizational procedures. 7. Participate in bed side clinical handovers and ensure continuity of care between shifts. Coordinate with relevant departments, including Emergency, IPD, OT, Pharmacy, Laboratory, SCANU/NICU, and referral services. Participate in team meetings, clinical reviews, emergency drills, and other relevant coordination activities. Support junior staff, assistants, or trainees through guidance and on-the-job learning when assigned. Ensure periodic sterilization of surgical instruments. job_description: Job Description: Midwife Lead– PHCC, Camp 5 & 12, Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar Position Summary The Midwife Lead will be responsible for providing technical and operational leadership for midwifery and maternal, newborn, reproductive, and sexual health services at the Primary Health Care Centre (PHCC) in the Rohingya Response. The position holder will ensure the delivery of safe, high-quality, respectful, timely, and patient-centred care in accordance with approved national guidelines, organizational protocols, and relevant health sector standards. The Midwife Lead will supervise and support Midwives and relevant maternity care staff, ensuring effective service delivery, appropriate clinical assessment and management, timely identification and referral of high-risk cases, quality documentation, patient safety, and continuity of care. The position holder will work closely with the Clinical In-Charge, Medical Officers, Nurses, Pharmacy, Laboratory, Nutrition, MHPSS, Community Health, and other relevant teams. Duty Station: Camp 5 & 12, Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar Reports to: Senior Medical Officer Accountable to: Clinical Coordinator Key Responsibilities 1. Technical Leadership & Supervision Provide technical leadership, guidance, and supportive supervision to Midwives and relevant maternity care staff. Ensure that maternal, newborn, reproductive, and sexual health services are delivered according to approved clinical guidelines, protocols, and standards. Develop and maintain duty rosters and support effective allocation of Midwifery staff based on service needs. Conduct regular supportive supervision, observation, case review, and performance monitoring. Identify technical gaps and provide on-the-job coaching and mentoring to Midwives. Support orientation and capacity building of newly recruited Midwives and relevant clinical staff. Promote teamwork, accountability, professional ethics, and respectful maternity care. 2. Maternal & Newborn Health Services Ensure the provision of high-quality antenatal, intrapartum, postnatal, and essential newborn care within the PHCC service package. Ensure appropriate assessment, monitoring, counselling, and follow-up of pregnant women and newborns. Support the identification and management of common maternal and newborn health conditions within the capacity of the facility. Ensure timely identification of high-risk pregnancies, maternal complications, newborn danger signs, and other emergency conditions. Ensure appropriate stabilization and timely referral of complicated maternal and newborn cases. Promote continuity of care through appropriate follow-up and coordination with referral facilities. Ensure respectful, dignified, confidential, and non-discriminatory care for women and newborns. 3. Labour, Delivery & Emergency Obstetric Care Lead and support Midwives in the provision of safe and respectful labour and delivery care, where delivery services are included within the PHCC service package. Ensure appropriate monitoring of labour and timely identification of abnormal labour or maternal and fetal distress. Ensure the appropriate use of relevant clinical tools and documentation during labour and delivery. Support the initial management and stabilization of obstetric and newborn emergencies within the scope and capacity of the facility. Ensure timely escalation, consultation, and referral of cases requiring higher-level care. Participate in emergency drills, preparedness activities, and review of maternal and newborn emergencies. Ensure appropriate documentation of emergency management, referrals, and outcomes. 4. Sexual & Reproductive Health and Family Planning Ensure the delivery of appropriate sexual and reproductive health services within the approved PHCC service package. Provide technical support for family planning counselling and service provision. Ensure clients receive informed, voluntary, confidential, and non-discriminatory family planning services. Support counselling on available family planning methods, benefits, potential side effects, and follow-up requirements. Ensure appropriate referral for services that are not available at the PHCC. Promote informed decision-making and respect for clients' choices and reproductive rights. 5. Clinical Assessment, Triage & Referral Ensure appropriate assessment and prioritization of pregnant women, mothers, newborns, and other clients requiring Midwifery services. Identify danger signs, high-risk pregnancies, obstetric complications, and newborn emergencies. Ensure immediate attention and appropriate stabilization of emergency cases within the facility's capacity. Coordinate with the Clinical In-Charge, Medical Officers, and other relevant staff for complicated cases. Ensure timely referral to appropriate higher-level facilities when required. Ensure accurate completion of referral documentation and communication of relevant clinical information. Support follow-up of referred patients where applicable. 6. Clinical Quality & Patient Safety Ensure Midwifery services comply with approved national treatment guidelines, standard operating procedures, and organizational clinical protocols. Promote evidence-based practices and high standards of maternal and newborn care. Participate in clinical audits, maternal and newborn death reviews, case reviews, and quality improvement activities, where applicable. Identify clinical risks, patient safety concerns, or gaps in service delivery and report them to the appropriate supervisor. Support the development and implementation of corrective actions and quality improvement initiatives. Promote respectful maternity care and protect the dignity, privacy, and rights of women and newborns. Support measures to prevent medical errors and improve patient safety. 7. Infection Prevention & Control (IPC) Ensure adherence to Infection Prevention and Control procedures within maternity and Midwifery service areas. Promote appropriate hand hygiene, standard precautions, and use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Ensure safe and clean practices during maternal, newborn, and reproductive health service delivery. Identify and report IPC risks, gaps, or incidents. Support the implementation of IPC measures during disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies. Ensure appropriate coordination with relevant teams regarding waste management and environmental cleanliness. 8. Medicines, Medical Supplies & Equipment Ensure the appropriate use of medicines, medical supplies, and equipment related to Midwifery and maternal-newborn health services. Work closely with the Pharmacy and Supply Chain teams to monitor the availability of essential medicines and reproductive health commodities. Report shortages, stock-outs, near-expiry items, or equipment gaps that may affect service delivery. Ensure appropriate use and basic maintenance of relevant Midwifery and newborn care equipment. Report damaged, malfunctioning, or unsafe equipment to the appropriate department. Support the rational use of medicines and medical supplies. 9. Clinical Documentation & Patient Records Ensure accurate, complete, confidential, and timely documentation of maternal, newborn, and reproductive health services. Ensure appropriate maintenance of antenatal, postnatal, delivery, family planning, referral, and other relevant registers. Review documentation practices and address gaps through supportive supervision. Ensure accurate recording of assessments, treatment, counselling, referrals, and follow-up. Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with organizational data protection procedures. Support the accurate recording of service delivery information for reporting purposes. 10. Health Information, Reporting & Surveillance Ensure accurate and timely recording of maternal, newborn, and reproductive health service data. Review relevant registers and reports to ensure completeness and accuracy. Support the preparation of daily, weekly, monthly, and other required reports. Work closely with the MIS and programme teams to ensure data quality, completeness, and timely submission. Report maternal, newborn, or public health events according to applicable reporting procedures. Identify trends, service gaps, or quality concerns and communicate them to the appropriate supervisor. Maintain confidentiality of patient and programme information. 11. Coordination & Multidisciplinary Teamwork Work closely with the Clinical In-Charge, Medical Officers, Nurses, Pharmacy, Laboratory, Nutrition, MHPSS, Community Health, and other relevant teams. Coordinate patient care, referrals, follow-up, and continuity of maternal and newborn health services. Participate in clinical meetings, case discussions, programme review meetings, and coordination meetings. Coordinate with referral facilities and relevant service providers when required. Communicate technical concerns, staffing challenges, service delivery gaps, and patient safety issues to the supervisor. Promote effective communication and collaboration among maternity and other healthcare teams. 12. Capacity Building & Professional Development Identify training and capacity-building needs among Midwives and relevant maternity care staff. Conduct or support on-the-job coaching, mentoring, refresher sessions, and clinical orientation. Support knowledge sharing and continuous learning within the Midwifery team. Maintain updated knowledge of relevant maternal, newborn, reproductive health, and humanitarian health guidelines. Participate in relevant training, workshops, clinical meetings, and professional development activities. Promote a culture of continuous quality improvement and professional accountability. 13. Emergency Preparedness & Humanitarian Response Maintain readiness to ensure continuity of maternal, newborn, and reproductive health services during disease outbreaks, fires, natural disasters, mass casualty incidents, and other humanitarian emergencies. Support preparedness planning for maternal and newborn emergencies. Participate in emergency drills and response activities. Ensure appropriate availability and readiness of essential Midwifery equipment and emergency supplies. Support the continuation of essential services during emergencies and operational disruptions. Remain flexible to undertake additional responsibilities based on emergency and programme requirements. The position holder will ensure proper dispensing, patient counselling, medicine storage, stock management, inventory control, documentation, maintain digital consumption tool, and quality compliance with approved national & WHO guidelines, organizational policies, GMT guidelines and relevant health sector standards. The Pharmacist will work closely with Medical Officers, Nurses, Midwives, and other relevant healthcare staff to ensure the continuous availability and appropriate use of essential medicines and medical supplies, while maintaining high standards of patient safety, quality of care, and accountability. KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:   Pharmacy Service & Medicine Dispensing Ensure safe, accurate, timely, and appropriate dispensing of prescribed medicines to patients. Review prescriptions for completeness, appropriateness, dosage, frequency, duration, and potential medication-related concerns within the scope of practice. Verify patient details and ensure that the correct medicine, strength, dosage, and quantity are dispensed. Provide clear counselling to patients and caregivers regarding medicine use, dosage, administration, duration, possible side effects, precautions, and storage. Ensure proper labelling and packaging of medicines before dispensing. Maintain confidentiality and ensure respectful, equitable, and patient-centered pharmacy services. Promote patient understanding and adherence to prescribed treatment. Prescription Review & Rational Use of Medicines Support the rational and appropriate use of medicines in accordance with approved treatment guidelines and protocols. Identify potential prescription errors, inappropriate doses, duplication, contraindications, or other medicine-related concerns and communicate with the prescriber for clarification. Promote appropriate use of antibiotics and other priority medicines. Support measures to reduce medication errors and improve patient safety. Participate in activities related to rational medicine use, Pharmacovigilance and ADR reporting, antimicrobial stewardship, and quality improvement as applicable. Medicine & Medical Supply Management Maintain appropriate stock levels of medicines and essential medical supplies required for PHCC services. Monitor stock availability and ensure timely identification and reporting of shortages or potential stock-outs. Receive, inspect, verify, and properly document medicines and medical supplies received by the pharmacy. Ensure appropriate storage conditions according to manufacturer requirements and organizational procedures. Maintain proper arrangement of medicines using applicable stock management principles, including First Expiry, First Out (FEFO). Regularly monitor expiry dates and take appropriate action to prevent the dispensing of expired or damaged medicines. Ensure safe segregation and management of expired, damaged, recalled, or unusable medicines according to approved procedures. Conduct regular physical stock counts and reconcile stock balances with stock records. Inventory Control & Documentation Maintain accurate and up-to-date pharmacy stock cards, bin cards, registers, and other required inventory records. Ensure timely recording of medicine receipts, issues, transfers, adjustments, losses, expiries, and returns. Conduct routine stock reconciliation and investigate discrepancies. Maintain proper documentation of controlled or restricted medicines, where applicable, according to relevant policies and regulations. Support periodic inventory checks, audits, and physical verification of pharmacy stock. Ensure all pharmacy records are complete, accurate, and available for review. The position holder will support day-to-day administrative activities, logistics coordination, documentation, filing, asset and inventory management, transport arrangements, procurement follow-up, facility maintenance, and other operational requirements. The Assistant Officer – Admin & Logistics will work under the supervision of the Senior Officer – Admin & Logistics and closely coordinate with the Clinical Coordinator, Medical Officer Lead, Medical Warehouse, Pharmacy, Laboratory, Nursing, Midwifery, IPC, Surveillance, Finance, HR, Procurement, Supply Chain, Security, WASH, and other relevant teams to support uninterrupted and effective PHCC service delivery. Duty Station:  Camp 5 & 21, Cox’s Bazar Reports to: Senior Officer Admin & Logistics Accountable to: Deputy Project Coordinator KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY: Administrative Support Provide day-to-day administrative support to PHCC operations. Assist in preparing letters, notices, memos, meeting minutes, and other official documents. Maintain proper filing systems for administrative and operational documents. Support the preparation and distribution of internal communications. Maintain and organize electronic and physical records. Assist in scheduling meetings and coordinating administrative arrangements. Support follow-up of routine administrative action points. Receive and distribute official documents and correspondence as assigned. Maintain confidentiality of organizational and staff information. Meeting, Training & Event Support Support logistical arrangements for meetings, trainings, workshops, and orientations. Prepare meeting rooms and ensure required materials are available. Assist with participant registration and attendance records. Support preparation and distribution of meeting materials. Assist in documenting meeting minutes and action points when assigned. Coordinate refreshments and other approved logistical arrangements. Support follow-up on agreed action points. Ensure training and meeting venues are properly arranged. Logistics Coordination Support Provide day-to-day logistical support for PHCC activities. Assist in coordinating the movement and delivery of approved supplies and materials. Follow up on routine logistical requests. Coordinate with relevant teams regarding operational requirements. Support timely delivery of non-medical supplies to designated locations. Assist in tracking pending logistical requests. Report delays or logistical constraints to the Senior Officer – Admin & Logistics. Support logistics arrangements for programme and emergency activities. Procurement Request & Follow-up Support Assist PHCC teams in preparing procurement requests according to organizational procedures. Ensure requests contain required specifications and supporting documents. Maintain a tracking record of submitted procurement requests. Follow up with Procurement and Supply Chain teams regarding request status. Communicate updates on approved requests to relevant teams. Support receiving and checking of general supplies and equipment. Maintain relevant procurement-related records. Escalate delayed or urgent requests to the supervisor. Asset Management Support Assist in maintaining accurate PHCC asset records. Support asset tagging and registration. Maintain asset movement and handover records. Assist in periodic physical verification of assets. Monitor the location and condition of assigned assets. Report damaged, missing, or lost assets promptly. Support asset handover and return processes. Maintain supporting documentation related to assets. Assist during asset audits and verification exercises. General Store & Non-Medical Supply Management Assist in maintaining stock records for general office and non-medical supplies. Monitor the availability of stationery, office materials, cleaning supplies, and other approved non-medical items. Support proper storage and organization of supplies. Assist in receiving and issuing general supplies. Maintain stock issue and receipt records. Support periodic physical stock counts. Report shortages, damaged items, and stock discrepancies. Support timely replenishment of essential non-medical supplies. Transport & Movement Support Assist in coordinating transport requests for PHCC staff and activities. Maintain transport request records. Support communication with drivers and transport focal persons. Assist with scheduling approved staff movement and field visits. Follow up on vehicle availability. Communicate transport schedules to relevant staff. Support emergency transportation arrangements when assigned. Report transport constraints or delays to the supervisor. Facility & Office Support Support routine monitoring of PHCC offices and common operational areas. Identify basic maintenance and repair requirements. Report facility-related concerns to the Senior Officer – Admin & Logistics. Assist in following up on maintenance and repair requests. Monitor basic office and facility requirements, including furniture and equipment. Support arrangements for workspace and office facilities. Assist in maintaining a clean, organized, and functional working environment. Report damaged or unsafe equipment and facilities promptly. Utilities & Operational Services Support monitoring of essential operational services, including: o Electricity and backup power. o Water supply. o Lighting. o Ventilation. o Communication and internet services, where applicable. Report service interruptions or technical problems promptly. Assist in following up with relevant teams for restoration of services. Maintain relevant operational records when assigned. Support contingency arrangements during utility disruptions. Documentation & Record Management Maintain accurate and organized administrative and logistics records. Support proper filing of: o Procurement requests. o Asset records. o General stock records. o Transport requests. o Maintenance requests. o Meeting records. o Visitor records. o Administrative correspondence. Maintain both electronic and physical filing systems. Ensure documents are properly labelled and accessible to authorized personnel. Maintain confidentiality and security of organizational documents. Visitor & Reception Support Support the administrative management of official visitors. Maintain visitor records where applicable. Assist with arrangements for official meetings and visits. Provide basic administrative support during monitoring and official visits. Coordinate logistical arrangements for visitors when assigned. Ensure relevant staff are informed about scheduled official visits. Support appropriate access procedures for visitors. Coordination with PHCC Teams Work closely with the Senior Officer – Admin & Logistics and other PHCC teams. Coordinate with Pharmacy, Medical Warehouse, Laboratory, Nursing, Midwifery, IPC, Surveillance, and other teams regarding routine administrative and logistics requirements. Liaise with HR, Finance, Procurement, Supply Chain, Security, and other support departments. Support communication and follow-up between PHCC and support teams. Participate in relevant meetings when assigned. Communicate operational challenges and delays to the supervisor. Safety, Security & Health Support Follow organizational health, safety, and security procedures. Identify and report workplace hazards and unsafe conditions. Support basic facility safety measures. Ensure emergency exits and access routes are kept clear. Support the maintenance of safety notices and emergency information. Report security concerns promptly. Coordinate with Security and relevant teams when assigned. Support emergency preparedness activities. Emergency Preparedness & Humanitarian Response Support PHCC administrative and logistics operations during emergencies. Assist in mobilizing approved supplies and operational resources. Support logistics arrangements during disease outbreaks, fires, natural disasters, mass casualty incidents, and other emergencies. Assist with emergency transportation and movement arrangements when assigned. Support continuity of essential administrative and logistical services. Participate in emergency preparedness activities and drills. Remain flexible to undertake additional responsibilities during emergency response. Reporting & Follow-up Maintain routine updates on assigned administrative and logistics activities. Prepare basic tracking sheets and reports as required. Report pending requests, operational constraints, and significant issues to the supervisor. Support preparation of administrative and logistics reports. job_description: Job Description:  Medical Officer– PHCC, Camp 5 and 12 Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar. Position Summary The Medical Officer will be responsible for providing safe, high-quality, timely, and patient-centered medical care to patients attending the Primary Health Care Centre (PHCC) in the Rohingya Response, Cox’s Bazar. The position holder will conduct clinical assessments, diagnose and manage common health conditions, prescribe appropriate treatment, provide emergency care and initial stabilization, identify patients requiring referral, and ensure proper clinical documentation and follow-up. The Medical Officer will work under the technical guidance and supervision of the Medical Officer Lead/Clinical Coordinator and collaborate closely with Senior Medical Officers, Senior Staff Nurses, Staff Nurses, Midwife Lead, Midwives, Pharmacy, Laboratory, Nutrition, MHPSS, Community Health, and other relevant teams to ensure integrated and comprehensive primary healthcare services. Duty Station:  Camp 5 and 12 Ukhiya,Cox’s Bazar Reports to: Medical Officer Lead Accountable to: Senior Medical Officer KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:  1. Clinical Assessment & Patient Management ●	Provide safe, respectful, timely, and patient-centered medical care to patients attending the PHCC. ●	Conduct comprehensive patient assessments, including medical history taking and physical examinations. ●	Assess presenting complaints, identify relevant clinical signs and symptoms, danger sign and establish appropriate diagnosis. ●	Develop and implement appropriate treatment and management plans according to approved clinical guidelines. ●	Manage common acute and chronic medical conditions within the scope of PHCC services. ●	Monitor patient response to treatment and provide appropriate follow-up care for recurrent and chronic cases. ●	Identify patients requiring further investigation, observation, consultation, admission or referral. ●	Provide clear counselling to patients and caregivers regarding diagnosis, treatment, medication use, and follow-up. ●	Ensure patient dignity, privacy, confidentiality, informed consent, and non-discriminatory care at all times. 2. Primary Healthcare Service Delivery ●	Provide comprehensive primary healthcare services in accordance with the approved Essential Package of Health Services and facility capacity. ●	Diagnose and manage common communicable and non-communicable diseases. ●	Provide medical consultations for children, adolescents, adults, and older persons. ●	Support preventive healthcare, health education, and disease prevention activities. ●	Identify high-risk patients and ensure appropriate management or referral. ●	Support continuity of care for patients requiring follow-up. ●	Coordinate with relevant service providers to ensure integrated patient care. ●	Promote equitable access to quality healthcare services. 3. Clinical decision making - Diagnosis & Treatment ●	Conduct appropriate clinical assessments and establish provisional or final diagnoses. ●	Follow approved national clinical guidelines, standard treatment protocols, and organizational procedures. ●	Prescribe medicines safely, accurately, and rationally. ●	Request appropriate laboratory investigations based on clinical indications and available services. ●	Interpret available laboratory results and incorporate findings into patient management. ●	Monitor treatment outcomes and modify management plans when clinically appropriate. ●	Identify complications, treatment failure, or clinical deterioration requiring escalation or referral. ●	Provide appropriate medical advice and follow-up instructions. 4. Emergency Care & Initial Stabilization ●	Provide immediate medical assessment and management of patients presenting with emergency conditions like, -	Neonatal, pediatric and obstetric emergencies -	Management of different types of shock -	Management of acute respiratory illness -	Management of anaphylaxis, Seizures, severe hypoglycemia, severe dehydration, suspected acute coronary syndrome, stroke, Trauma, poisoning etc. ●	Identify danger signs and life-threatening conditions  ●	Provide initial emergency treatment and stabilization within the scope of practice and facility capacity. ●	Coordinate with nursing and other clinical staff during emergency situations. ●	Ensure timely escalation of critical cases to the Medical Officer Lead, Senior Medical Officer, Clinical Coordinator, or other appropriate personnel. ●	Support appropriate referral or transfer of critically ill patients. ●	Participate in emergency preparedness activities, drills, and response. ●	Ensure accurate documentation of emergency care and patient transfer. 5. Triage & Patient Prioritization ●	Support appropriate assessment and prioritization of patients according to clinical urgency. ●	Ensure patients with severe illness or danger signs receive immediate attention. ●	Identify patients requiring urgent intervention or referral. ●	Coordinate with nursing staff to support effective patient flow. ●	Monitor patients awaiting consultation when clinically necessary. ●	Escalate delays or clinical concerns that may affect patient safety. ●	Identify overcrowding and Support efficient patient flow and timely access to care. 6. Referral & Continuity of Care ●	Identify patients requiring referral to higher-level healthcare facilities. ●	Provide appropriate initial treatment and stabilization before referral. ●	Complete accurate and comprehensive referral documentation. ●	Ensure relevant clinical information accompanies the patient. ●	Provide counselling to patients and caregivers regarding referral procedures. ●	Coordinate with the Medical Officer Lead/Senior Medical Officer regarding complex or urgent referrals. ●	Support follow-up of referred patients when required. ●	Ensure appropriate continuity of care and follow-up. ●	Communicate effectively and handover about the patient to referral higher facility team. 7. Medication Management & Rational Prescribing ●	 Prescribe medicines according to approved clinical guidelines and protocols. ●	Ensure prescriptions are clear, accurate, complete, and legible. ●	Consider patient allergies, contraindications, and potential drug interactions. ●	Promote rational and evidence-based use of medicines, avoidance of unnecessary antibiotics ●	Monitor patients for adverse drug reactions or treatment-related complications and document allergies. ●	Coordinate with Pharmacy staff regarding medicine availability and medication-related concerns. ●	Report medication errors, adverse drug reactions, and other medication-related incidents according to organizational procedures. ●	Support appropriate counselling on medication use and adherence. 8. Communicable Disease Management ●	Diagnose and manage common communicable diseases according to approved national guidelines. ●	Identify patients with suspected infectious diseases requiring special precautions. ●	Ensure appropriate clinical management and referral when necessary. ●	Identify unusual disease patterns or suspected disease clusters. ●	Report suspected outbreaks, unusual health events, or notifiable diseases through appropriate channels. ●	Support disease prevention, control measures and support outbreak investigations. ●	Coordinate with Laboratory, Nursing, Community Health, and relevant teams during disease outbreaks. 9. Non-Communicable Disease (NCD) Management ●	Screen, diagnose, and manage common non-communicable diseases within the scope of PHCC services. ●	Provide counselling regarding lifestyle modification according to risk factor and disease prevention. ●	Support continuity of care for patients with chronic conditions. ●	Monitor treatment response and medication adherence. ●	Identify complications or poorly controlled conditions requiring referral. ●	Maintain appropriate documentation and follow-up records. 10. Maternal, Newborn & Child Health Support ●	Work closely with the Midwife Lead, Midwives, Nurses, and other relevant healthcare providers. ●	Provide medical assessment and management of pregnancy-related conditions within the scope of PHCC services. ●	Identify obstetric danger signs and ensure immediate management and referral. ●	Support emergency management of maternal complications until appropriate referral. ●	Assess and manage sick children according to approved guidelines. ●	Identify pediatric danger signs and emergencies. ●	Support appropriate referral of high-risk mothers, newborns, and children. ●	Participate in relevant maternal, newborn, and child health case discussions. 11. Infection Prevention & Control (IPC) ●	Follow and promote Infection Prevention and Control procedures in all assigned clinical areas. ●	Ensure adherence to hand hygiene and standard precautions. ●	Use Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) appropriately. ●	Support appropriate infection prevention measures during patient assessment and treatment. ●	Identify and report IPC risks, breaches, or gaps. ●	Support appropriate cleaning, disinfection, and safe clinical practices. ●	Follow relevant IPC procedures during disease outbreaks and public health emergencies. 12. Patient Safety & Clinical Quality ●	Ensure medical care is provided according to approved national guidelines, organizational protocols, and professional standards. ●	Promote evidence-based and patient-centred clinical practices. ●	Identify clinical risks, unsafe practices, and patient safety concerns. ●	Report adverse events, clinical incidents, and near misses through appropriate channels. ●	Participate in clinical audits, case reviews, supportive supervision, and quality improvement activities. ●	Implement recommendations and corrective actions as directed. ●	Promote a culture of patient safety, accountability, learning, and continuous improvement. 13. Clinical Documentation & Patient Records ●	Maintain accurate, complete, timely, and confidential patient records. ●	Document patient history, examination findings, diagnosis, treatment plans, prescriptions, investigations, and follow-up instructions. ●	Complete referral and transfer documentation accurately. ●	Maintain relevant clinical registers and records. ●	Ensure patient information is kept confidential. ●	Follow organizational data protection and record management procedures. ●	Address documentation gaps identified through supervision or record reviews. 14. Coordination with Multidisciplinary Teams ●	Work closely with the Medical Officer Lead, Senior Medical Officers, Clinical Coordinator, Nursing team, Midwife Lead, Midwives, Pharmacy, Laboratory, Nutrition, MHPSS, and Community Health teams. ●	Coordinate patient investigations, treatment, referrals, and follow-up. ●	Ensure appropriate communication between relevant healthcare providers. ●	Participate in clinical meetings, case discussions, and programme review meetings. ●	Communicate clinical concerns and service delivery challenges to the appropriate supervisor. ●	Promote effective teamwork and professional communication. ●	Support integrated and multidisciplinary patient care. 15. Medicines, Medical Supplies & Equipment ●	Use medicines, medical supplies, and equipment responsibly and appropriately. ●	Report shortages, stock-outs, damaged items, or unsafe equipment promptly. ●	Coordinate with Pharmacy and relevant teams regarding clinical requirements. ●	Ensure appropriate care, maintenance and use of medical equipment with checking expiry date where assigned. ●	Support regular checking of emergency equipment, essential supplies and reporting malfunctioning equipment. ●	Promote rational use and proper accountability of medical supplies. 16. Health Information & Reporting ●	Ensure accurate recording of patient consultations and clinical activities. ●	Maintain relevant clinical registers and service delivery records. ●	Support preparation of daily, weekly, monthly, and other required reports. ●	Ensure clinical information is complete, accurate, and submitted on time. ●	Report unusual disease patterns, suspected outbreaks, and significant public health concerns. ●	Maintain confidentiality of patient and programme information. 17. Capacity Building & Professional Development ●	Participate in clinical orientations, training, refresher sessions, case discussions, and professional development activities. ●	Maintain updated knowledge of national clinical guidelines and organizational protocols. ●	Participate in clinical learning and quality improvement initiatives. ●	Share relevant clinical knowledge with colleagues. ●	Apply updated clinical guidance and best practices in daily work. ●	Support the orientation of new staff when assigned. 18. Emergency Preparedness & Humanitarian Response ●	Maintain readiness to provide medical services during disease outbreaks, fires, natural disasters, mass casualty incidents, and other humanitarian emergencies. ●	Participate in emergency preparedness activities, drills, and simulations. ●	Support continuity of essential healthcare services during emergencies. ●	Provide medical care during emergency response activities. ●	Assist in the assessment, stabilization, and referral of emergency patients. ●	Remain flexible to undertake additional responsibilities based on emergency and programme requirements. The role holder may be required to undertake additional duties reasonably related to their qualifications, skills, and experience, based on programme and operational requirements. job_description: Position Summary The Assistant Officer – MIS will be responsible for supporting the effective collection, compilation, entry, verification, analysis, management, and reporting of programme and health service data for the Primary Health Care Centre (PHCC) under the Rohingya Response. The position holder will ensure that data and information are accurate, complete, timely, consistent, and properly maintained in accordance with organizational procedures, donor requirements, relevant health information standards, and data protection principles. The Assistant Officer – MIS will work closely with the Clinical In-Charge, Medical Officers, Nurses, Midwives, Pharmacy, Laboratory, Nutrition, MHPSS, Community Health, MEAL, and other relevant programme and support teams to ensure quality data management and timely reporting for programme monitoring, decision-making, and accountability. Duty Station:  Camp 5 ,12 & 21, Cox’s Bazar. Reports to: MIS Officer Accountable to: MIS Manager Data Collection & Compilation Collect, compile, and consolidate programme and health service data from relevant service delivery points and departments. Ensure the timely collection of daily, weekly, monthly, and other required data. Review source documents, registers, tally sheets, and reporting formats for completeness before data entry. Follow up with relevant staff to obtain missing, incomplete, or unclear information. Maintain an organized system for collecting and compiling data from different PHCC service areas. Support the consolidation of service delivery information for internal and external reporting requirements. Data Entry & Database Management Enter programme and health service data accurately and timely into approved databases, MIS platforms, spreadsheets, or other information management systems. Update relevant trackers, databases, and reporting tools regularly. Maintain accurate electronic records and ensure appropriate backup of MIS data. Organize and manage electronic files, folders, and databases according to approved procedures. Ensure consistency between source documents, registers, databases, and summary reports. Support the maintenance and updating of programme information management systems. Data Quality Assurance & Validation Conduct routine data quality checks to identify missing, duplicate, inconsistent, inaccurate, or unusual data. Verify data against source documents and coordinate with relevant service providers to correct identified discrepancies. Support routine data cleaning, validation, and reconciliation. Maintain records of identified data quality issues and corrective actions taken. Support the implementation of data quality improvement measures. Ensure that data submitted for reporting are complete, accurate, and validated. Health Information & Service Delivery Reporting Support the preparation of daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and other required programme and health service reports. Compile service delivery data from OPD, Nursing, Midwifery, Pharmacy, Laboratory, Nutrition, MHPSS, Community Health, and other relevant departments. Prepare summary tables, data trackers, charts, and other reporting formats as required. Ensure reports are submitted accurately and within established deadlines. Support the preparation of internal management reports and donor reporting requirements. Maintain records of submitted reports and reporting deadlines. Data Analysis & Information Management Support basic analysis of programme and service delivery data to identify trends, gaps, and unusual patterns. Prepare summary statistics, tables, graphs, and visual presentations for programme review and decision-making. Assist in monitoring key performance indicators and programme targets. Support the development and updating of dashboards, trackers, and other data visualization tools. Identify significant changes, unusual trends, or potential data concerns and communicate them to the appropriate supervisor. Provide timely and accurate information to support programme planning and performance monitoring. Coordination with Clinical & Programme Teams Work closely with the Clinical In-Charge, Medical Officers, Nurses, Midwives, Pharmacy, Laboratory, Nutrition, MHPSS, Community Health, and other programme teams. Provide technical support to relevant staff regarding data collection tools, registers, reporting formats, and data entry requirements. Coordinate with department focal persons to ensure timely submission of required data. Follow up on missing reports, incomplete data, and reporting delays. Participate in programme meetings, data review meetings, and other relevant coordination meetings. Communicate data quality issues, reporting gaps, and system-related challenges to the appropriate supervisor. Data Confidentiality & Protection Maintain strict confidentiality of patient, beneficiary, staff, and programme information. Ensure appropriate access control and secure handling of sensitive data. Follow organizational data protection, confidentiality, and information management procedures. Ensure electronic and physical data are stored securely. Avoid unauthorized sharing, copying, or disclosure of confidential information. Immediately report any suspected data breach, loss, or unauthorized access to the appropriate supervisor. Documentation & Record Management Maintain organized electronic and physical MIS-related documentation. Ensure reporting formats, source documents, databases, and trackers are properly maintained. Support the archiving and retrieval of programme data and reports. Maintain version control of key reporting formats and databases where applicable. Ensure relevant documentation is available for management review, audits, donor verification, and programme monitoring. Support proper document retention according to organizational procedures. Monitoring, MEAL & Programme Support Support MEAL and programme teams with routine data compilation and reporting. Assist in tracking programme indicators, targets, achievements, and service delivery performance. Support data collection for programme monitoring, assessments, surveys, and other relevant activities when required. Assist in compiling information required for donor reports and programme reviews. Support routine monitoring of data completeness, reporting timeliness, and indicator performance. Contribute to identifying data-related gaps and supporting practical improvement measures. System & Digital Tool Support Support the use and maintenance of approved MIS platforms, databases, digital data collection tools, and reporting systems. Provide basic troubleshooting support to users experiencing routine data entry or reporting issues. Escalate technical or system-related problems to the appropriate IT or MIS focal point. Support staff orientation on approved data collection and reporting tools. Assist with system updates, data migration, or database maintenance as assigned. Maintain accurate user and access-related records where applicable and authorized. Audit, Compliance & Data Verification Support Support internal and external reviews by preparing relevant reports, datasets, and supporting documentation. Assist in responding to data-related queries from management, programme teams, auditors, donors, or other authorized stakeholders. Participate in routine data verification, spot checks, and data quality assessments. Support the implementation of recommendations arising from data reviews, audits, and monitoring activities. Ensure data management practices comply with organizational policies and reporting requirements. Capacity Building & Professional Development Participate in training, orientation, data review meetings, and professional development activities. Maintain updated knowledge of relevant health information systems, data management practices, and reporting requirements. Support basic orientation and guidance for staff on data collection and reporting procedures. Participate in knowledge-sharing and continuous learning activities. Follow updates to organizational MIS procedures, reporting formats, and relevant programme requirements. Emergency Preparedness & Humanitarian Response Support the timely collection, compilation, and reporting of information during disease outbreaks, fires, natural disasters, mass casualty incidents, and other humanitarian emergencies. Assist in maintaining emergency data trackers and reporting systems. Support rapid data compilation for emergency response planning and decision-making. Ensure the continuity and security of essential programme information during emergencies. Remain flexible to undertake additional MIS and information management responsibilities based on emergency and programme requirements.
